# Cloud Coding Agent Starter Pack

> Open, source-linked guide that teaches developers how to run and manage AI coding agents in the cloud. Covers 15 terminal coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor CLI, OpenCode, Pi, OMP, Devin CLI, Aider, Amp, Crush, Factory Droid, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, goose, Qwen Code): how to install each on a server, authenticate without a browser, run it headlessly with permission prompts off, get JSON output, and its cloud-specific gotchas. Also compares 12 platforms to run them on: Northflank Cloud Harness, Claude Code on the web, OpenAI Codex cloud, Cursor Cloud Agents, GitHub Copilot cloud agent, GitHub Codespaces, Ona (formerly Gitpod), Coder, E2B, Daytona, Sprites (Fly.io) and Modal Sandboxes. Covers supported agents, isolation, persistence, session limits, SSH/IDE access, BYOC and cost for standard agent workloads, plus runnable setups. Last verified 2026-10-19. Maintained by Northflank.

## Main pages
- [README](README.md): agents, one-line headless commands, where to run them, cost by workload, FAQ
- [Agent comparison](agents/README.md): install, headless command, permissions, JSON output, resume, models, auth, instruction files, sandboxing and MCP for every agent
- [Feature matrix](comparisons/feature-matrix.md): agents, isolation, lifecycle, access, network, BYOC
- [Pricing](comparisons/pricing.md): per-hour rates, subscription pricing, hidden costs
- [Methodology](methodology.md): sources, normalisation, formula, limitations
